brief:
Children named Mira and Ahed are recording temperatures inside their tent reaching 42°C (107.6°F) amid worsening humanitarian conditions in the Gaza Strip, Eye on Palestine reported. Their documentation captures the daily reality facing displaced children as canvas and fabric shelters provide minimal protection against extreme heat in the region.

The children's account reflects broader conditions affecting displaced populations across Gaza, where inadequate shelter compounds existing humanitarian hardship. Displacement camps have struggled with basic infrastructure as living conditions deteriorate, leaving families vulnerable to weather extremes and disease. The temperature readings underscore the physical toll of displacement on children during summer months in the territory.
